exposure: Duration of prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) to labor induction protocol (12 hours vs. 24 hours)
cohort: The study included 1764 women with term prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM) who underwent either a 12-hour or a 24-hour induction of labor protocol, with a subgroup analysis of women with a previous cesarean delivery.
finding: A 24-hour PROM-to-induction protocol led to a higher rate of spontaneous labor but also increased rates of chorioamnionitis, NICU admission, antibiotic administration, and neonatal respiratory distress compared to a 12-hour protocol.
mod_finding: The overall cesarean delivery rate was similar between the two groups, but among women with a previous CD, longer expectant management (24-hour protocol) resulted in significantly lower induction and CD rates.
